column1: # Copied from otfabric/iec60870-5-interop tests/iec103/known-bugs-consumer.tsv at v0.4.0 (contract 2.3).
# Known bugs of upstream versions for IEC 60870-5-103 that no pairing of this
# harness shows, because the only server here (vitusdong) shares or lacks the
# behaviour: they were seen on the wire against a consumer's own station or
# the frames are in docs/COMPATIBILITY.md). Same columns as known-bugs.tsv.
# scripts/interop.sh does not read this file (an entry here cannot reproduce
# in the harness and would be reported stale); consumers apply it together
# with known-bugs.tsv. The clause numbers are those of IEC 60870-5-103:1997.

column4: Iec103Client sends the generic read command (ASDU 21, cause 42) and the generic write command (ASDU 10, cause 40) with INF 0 instead of an information number of table 18 (244 read single entry, 250 write with execution), e.g. 15 81 2A 01 FE 00 01 01 01 03 01; a station that serves only the information numbers of the standard does not answer

Iec103Server answers a generic read and a generic write with ASDU 10 INF 0 instead of the INF of the command (244, 250; clause 7.4.8.6, figures 16 and 17), and acknowledges a write with execution with a data set carrying a reply code (0A 81 28 01 FE 00 01 01 01 02 01 16 01 01 00) where clause 7.4.8.6.3 has no data sets for cause 40

Iec103Server sends the list of recorded disturbances as ASDU 23 with VSQ 81 (SQ 1; clause 7.3.1.11: SQ 0 and the number of faults), function type 255 whatever the order's and the device's function type, and SOF with TP in bit 8 (80 for a trip; clause 7.2.6.24: TP is bit 1): 17 81 1F 01 FF 00 07 00 80 0C 00 1E 0F 09 0A 1A
Iec103Client decodes SOF with TP, TM, TEST and OTEV in bits 8 to 5 instead of 1 to 4 (clause 7.2.6.24), so a fault recorded with a trip (SOF 01) is reported without one

Iec103Client.ReadDisturbance acknowledges the whole disturbance data as transmitted (ASDU 25, TOO 64) right after the ASDU 26, then requests the disturbance data (TOO 2) and waits for an ASDU 27 for every channel at once; clause 7.4.7 (figure 10) has the request answered by ASDU 28, the tags, the channels offered one by one, and TOO 64 only after the end of the disturbance data (TOO 32). A station that follows the clause ends the transfer at the early TOO 64 and answers the TOO 2 with TOO 34

IEC8705103Manager reads ASDU 30 through struct ASDU30 {TOV, FAN[2], ACC, NDV, unsigned short NFE} without packing, so NFE is read from the octet after it and the low octet of the first value (alignment padding), and the values of every ASDU 30 but one whose NFE is below 256 and whose first value has a zero low octet are stored at the wrong position: of the fixture's channels only the first 25 values of channel 1 arrive where they belong. The procedure itself (ASDUs 24 and 25 with TOO 1, 2, 16, 68, 8, 66, 64) follows clause 7.4.7
